text:
maria: Heads up - we're seeing a sudden spike in preemptible evictions in us-west1 over the last 10m. Affects mixed-capacity pools for gpu-models tier=low.
aj: Saw it. eviction-rate metric jumped to ~22% at 12:02 PDT. p95 latency for low-tier requests increased from 110ms -> 260ms.
kevin: Any network blips or maintenance in us-west1? cloud console shows no scheduled maintenance.
sasha: I think it's spot churn, not network. Preemptible availability dropped across all zones in the region. Logs show lots of instance-termination events.
maria: Correct. This is primarily spot churn. Impact: low-tier customers (non-SLA) losing inference capacity and backfilling is causing throttles in higher tiers.
devon: TL;DR: propose two-stage fallback: 1) spill to local dedicated GPU warm pool (if available), 2) failover to regional cheaper on-demand CPU variant for non-latency-sensitive requests.
aj: Can we do partial model-variant fallback instead of full region failover? e.g., route to smaller/quantized variant (4-bit) before region failover.
maria: Yes, prefer model-variant fallback to region failover to keep egress/regulatory constraints local.
kevin: Agreed. Policy I suggest:
- If eviction_rate > 10% AND available_gpu_free < 5%: 1) degrade to q4_256 variant for low-tier; 2) enable aggressive batching window for queued requests; 3) only if GPU warm pool < 10% then region fanout.
sasha: We need to respect customer tiers: premium should always get dedicated on-demand first. low-tier gets model-fallback then CPU fallback.
devon: Also add a jittered backoff on requeue to avoid stampedes. current requeue is immediate, causing thundering herd.
aj: Ops-bot snapshot:
```
ops-bot: region=us-west1 eviction_rate=22.1% free_gpu=3.8% warm_pool=6 / active_pods=412
```
kevin: Proposed routing rule (pseudo):
```
if region.eviction_rate > 10%:
  route.low_tier -> model_variant(q4_256) until latency > target
  if warm_pool.available < 10%:
    route.low_tier -> cpu-region-local (best-effort)
  route.premium -> on_demand_gpu
```
aj: Where do we configure this? In the router policy repo or in fleet-agent remote flags?
maria: fleet-router policy with feature-flag rollout. We can flip on for us-west1 only.
sasha: Quick checklist:
1) implement variant-fallback in router (5 lines change)
2) add warm_pool thresholds to health signals
3) dropdown to regional fanout as last resort
4) add metric: fallback_rate_by_tier
5) postmortem window: 72h
kevin: I can send a PR for the router rule and add circuit-breaker thresholds.
devon: I'll update the agent to jitter requeue and cap retries to 3.
aj: Can we add a temporary autoscale burst to dedicated pool for low-tier for 15m to smooth traffic while variant-fallback ramps?
maria: Yes but budget ops: finance ok for 15m emergency burst if tagged "eviction-mitigation". @finance please ack.
kevin: For observability, add traces linking original request -> fallback path so we can measure quality regressions.
sasha: Also log reason_code in request headers: X-Fallback-Reason=eviction|warm_pool|latency
ops-bot: ACTION created: incident-1765432199, assignees=[kevin,devon], severity=medium
maria: Plan of record: roll out variant-fallback policy in canary (1 zone), enable jittered requeue, monitor p95 and fallback_rate for 30m, then widen if stable.
aj: I'll watch dashboards and post updates. If p95 for premium > 200ms we rollback.
kevin: PR link: https://git.redwood/repo/router/pulls/1823 (draft)
devon: Agent patch: https://git.redwood/repo/agents/pulls/407 (draft)
sasha: Thanks team. Small action items: kevin + devon to merge, maria to trigger feature flag canary, aj to monitor, i'll prepare postmortem template.
maria: Quick note — we should not region-failover customers with data-residency flags. keep local-only policies for them.
kevin: Noted. We'll add hard-exclusion zone on route:if customer.has_data_residency -> no region-fanout.
aj: Update in 18m: eviction rate dropping to 9.7% after warm-pool burst. p95 back to 130ms for low-tier.
maria: Closing loop: keep policy as default but add rollback timer 2h in case churn spikes again. Thanks :thumbsup:
